$:set -euo pipefail
printf '=== REQUIREMENTS FILE ===\n'
if test -f terminals_requirements.json; then cat terminals_requirements.json; else echo 'ABSENT'; fi
printf '\n=== PROGRAMS DESIGN INTERFACES HEAD ===\n'
sed -n '1,115p' workspaces/programs-srs-design/INTERFACES.md
printf '\n=== PROGRAMS DESIGN PATHS ===\n'
git ls-files workspaces/programs-srs-design
printf '\n=== REPO AND WORKTREE ===\n'
git rev-parse HEAD
git status --short
outputThat: "purpose": "Repository-level requirements for terminal operation contracts, software requirements specifications, and agent-oriented semantic projections.",
"SHALL": "Mandatory requirement; implementation and verification must satisfy it.",
"SHOULD": "Recommended procedure, subordinate to the mandatory requirements."
"shall": "The Terminals repository SHALL maintain an AGENTS.md that defines the mandatory rules and the procedures for operating every supported terminal surface.",
"verification": "AGENTS.md exists and covers the available terminal surfaces, their entry points, operation constraints, and verification."
"shall": "AGENTS.md SHALL keep mandatory imperatives separate from procedural instructions, express rules using SHALL, and organize procedures independently using SHOULD and actionable examples.",
"verification": "Mandatory rules and independently organized procedures are distinguishable, and procedure material does not weaken or replace a rule."
"shall": "The procedures in AGENTS.md SHALL collectively provide sufficient information to carry out every applicable imperative in their domain.",
"verification": "Each imperative can be executed through one or more documented procedures with required inputs, steps, outputs, and verification guidance."
"shall": "Every substantive application in scope SHALL have a Software Requirements Specification (SRS).",
"verification": "Each substantive application has an identifiable SRS artifact."

"shall": "An application's SRS SHALL be produced either as the primary specification before implementation or retrospectively after implementation; a retrospective SRS SHALL describe the as-implemented behavior and constraints.",
"verification": "The SRS identifies whether its relationship to implementation is prospective or retrospective, and its contents correspond to the relevant intended or implemented behavior."
"shall": "Every Markdown SRS SHALL be projected into an associated machine-readable specification intended for semantic agent consumption.",
"verification": "An associated machine-readable specification exists and identifies its Markdown source."

"shall": "The SRS projection SHALL transform source material into a semantics-first structure rather than perform a line-by-line mapping, preserve Markdown section order as an obligation, or merely serialize Markdown text.",
"verification": "Projection records are grouped and structured by semantic function and can be interpreted without reconstructing the Markdown document."
"shall": "The SRS projection SHALL preserve all source-supported information necessary for agents to understand, implement, operate, test, and verify the specified application.",

"verification": "All applicable requirements, contracts, actors, preconditions, inputs, outputs, invariants, state transitions, constraints, error behavior, dependencies, and acceptance criteria remain recoverable; absent concepts are not invented."

"shall": "The SRS projection SHALL use atomic and unambiguous requirements, stable identifiers, explicit relationships, consistent terms, typed structures, and task-oriented semantic grouping according to best practices for agent consumption.",
"verification": "Agents can identify actionable obligations, their subjects, dependencies, verification criteria, and associated contracts without relying on prose layout."

"shall": "The SRS projection SHALL preserve source intent and distinguish sourced facts, derived structure, interpretations, assumptions, and unresolved ambiguities without fabricating source requirements.",
"verification": "The projection identifies provenance and marks unresolved ambiguity explicitly instead of presenting an inference as a source requirement."

"shall": "Each SRS projection SHALL record source identity and revision, projection schema/version, and sufficient provenance for semantic traceability, and SHALL be revised when the source SRS changes materially.",
"verification": "Source and projection revisions can be identified, and material source changes produce an updated compatible projection or an explicit out-of-sync status."

"substantive_application": "An application with meaningful behavior, interfaces, data handling, execution semantics, state, or failure modes; its classification is independent of whether implementation preceded specification.",
"role": "Human explanation, review, and provenance; not the preferred operational representation for agent consumption."
"role": "Normalized, structured, actionable semantic representations that make application requirements and operational contracts directly consumable."
"target": "Machine-readable specification; JSON is the default representation unless a documented application contract specifies another machine-readable format.",
"equivalence": "Preserve implementation- and verification-relevant meaning, not the source document's physical lines, section sequence, typography, or prose phrasing.",

"transformation": "Extract and normalize semantic units; classify requirements and relationships; make conditions, types, boundaries, constraints, and verification explicit where supported; group by agent task and domain responsibility.",
"fidelity": "No substantive loss, silent scope reduction, unsupported requirement invention, or presentation-only copy masquerading as semantic projection."
# Programs — Interfaces, data shapes and state semantics
**Names:** Programs = new subsystem; RuntimeConfig = existing legacy files.
| 'request_json' | string | Yes | JSON serialization of exactly one {runpath,set} request |
| 'request_id' | string | No | Caller-supplied correlation key; must not authorize execution |

No GitHub Issue number, comment ID, or synthetic 'issue_comment' payload is required for a direct Programs dispatch. GitHub provides 'github.run_id', 'github.run_attempt', 'github.repository', 'github.ref' and 'github.actor'. An upstream adapter may retain independently verified Issue metadata in a separate trusted provenance record. A request cannot authorize itself by asserting its own 'source'.

This is a **proposed post-migration** example, not a request executable against the current tree. The existing writer program is at 'workspaces/RuntimeConfig/issue-body-writer/issue-body-writer.js'. The 'set' object must match the actual selected template exactly; the above shape is correct only for a template with 'jsPath' and those exact 'args' keys.
A dispatch request has no generic 'whatPrompt' or shell expression. It invokes the registered program's file via the Programs runner.
- Require a single JSON object, with exactly 'runpath' and 'set'.
- No additional top-level keys in the serialized request.
- 'runpath' points to one existing subfolder and a regular 'runtrigger.json'.
- The entire 'set' structure must match the selected template other than 'metadata'.
- Reject extra/missing keys, incompatible scalar types, empty values, malformed JSON, path escapes and missing program files.
- Validate trust and authorization separately from user-controlled request fields.
- Fail before program execution and before any durable clone on admission failure.

Each registered folder contains a template named 'runtrigger.json'. The runner may be shared outside those folders. Per-program entry points and argument names are not global contracts; a program may use any nested argument object that matches its template.
"jsonArrayPath": "<JSON array path or serialized JSON array>"

**Template ownership:** 'metadata' is retained without accepting corresponding request values. A generated clone is neither the template nor a writable shared configuration file. Runtime provenance and output state belong in a separate execution record unless a future schema explicitly allocates a runtime-owned namespace.

**Actual legacy spelling:** 'jsPath' (camelCase). Issue #10 narrative described 'js_path', which is incompatible with current 'runner.js'. Programs SHALL use the actual runner key and report discrepancies rather than guessing.
The runner validates a JSON object containing a usable 'jsPath' and an 'args' object, then invokes:

There is **one serialized JSON argument** to the selected program. The kernel does not expand arbitrary keys into multiple positional arguments. The selected program parses, validates, and interprets its own named args.

Required execution observations: child exit status; termination signal and runtime errors; stdout/stderr; time bounds; source revision; exact trigger path and digest. Any targeted resource mutation must be verified by the responsible program or a separate verifier.
The trigger instance's filename SHALL derive from the workflow run and attempt or equivalent unique run identity, not from a mandatory Issue source.

The source-controlled template stays at 'runtrigger.json'. The instance contains template 'metadata' plus all validated 'set' values. The *bytes of the trigger* must be committed and remotely read back before the runner starts. A commit SHA and digest identify the persisted instance.
A failed push or byte mismatch is a **pre-execution failure**. The runner must not execute based on locally present but remotely unverified content.
